⚡️ Negotiations are another battlefield; enemy lacks capacity for new war: IRGC spokesperson

📌 Tehran, IRNA — The spokesperson for the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) says Iran is fully prepared for war but can also pursue negotiations if national interests require, stressing that talks can constitute “another battlefield.”

“Negotiation does not mean compromise; negotiation is another scene of war,” Second Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbisaid said in an interview with IRNA on Tuesday, adding that while one form of war is conducted with weapons, negotiations involve “war with words, arguments and diplomatic methods.”
​
He said the IRGC has prepared itself for a prolonged war and that Iran’s Armed Forces are fully ready for war.
​
“What is correct in this matter is that we should have 100-percent readiness for war, and we have this capability and readiness. [Iranian] Armed Forces are now 100 percent ready to fight, and the IRGC has prepared itself for a long war. But this does not mean rejecting negotiations,” he said.
​
Mohebbi stressed that decisions on war and negotiations are not made by the IRGC alone, saying such decisions are made within the framework of Iran’s political system and under the command of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces.
​
The IRGC spokesperson also said Iran’s approach should be determined by national interests.
​
“We must see when and through what action our national interests are served. If our national interests require us to fight, we must fight. If our national interests require us to negotiate alongside the war, we must negotiate,” he said.
​
Mohebbi further noted that the recent US-Israeli war against Iran exposed what he described as weaknesses in the United States’ regional military posture, particularly regarding its military bases, intelligence capabilities and presence in the Persian Gulf.
​
He said Iran should maintain both military preparedness and the ability to use diplomacy, describing the two as complementary instruments in pursuing national interests.

🔊 Leader of Islamic Revolution offers condolences over passing of Ayatollah Shobeiri Zanjani

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Khamenei has issued a message of condolence over the passing of prominent Shia cleric and source of emulation Ayatollah Seyyed Mousa Shobeiri Zanjani.

The Leader issued the message on Tuesday, a day after Ayatollah Shobeiri Zanjani’s office announced his passing.
​
The following is the full text of Ayatollah Khamenei’s message, as shared by his official Telegram account:
​
In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful
​
The sorrowful news of the passing of the revered teacher and distinguished jurist, his eminence Grand Ayatollah Shobeiri Zanjani (may God be pleased with him) has been received.
​
Throughout his noble life, except for the first few years of childhood, this esteemed scholar devoted himself to learning, teaching, and scholarly research. He was consistently regarded by his peers, contemporaries, and teachers as a meticulous scholar and profound thinker. His mastery of the various disciplines pertaining to the derivation of Islamic legal rulings was accompanied by great subtlety and a careful consideration of the finest details.
​
The lessons he delivered, even when attended by no more than a handful of students, were renowned for their thorough research and meticulous analysis—and rightly so.
​
By the grace of God, over the course of slightly more than the past three decades, many people had the opportunity to benefit, according to their own capacity, from his invaluable presence and to draw from his knowledge for their own scholarly circles and teaching. His company was a source of both imparting and acquiring knowledge—even when, after his lessons, he would walk toward his home. Beyond his undisputed scholarly stature, his humble and fatherly manner toward students and scholars was also evident and deeply instructive.
​
Without doubt, the passing of this distinguished personality has left a void among the foremost Shia scholars of the present age, and filling this void may take a considerable length of time.
​
I extend my condolences for this grievous loss to our Master [Imam Mahdi], may God hasten his noble reappearance, to the Islamic seminaries, and especially to his students and admirers, and most particularly to his noble household, a family that has nurtured generations of scholars and learned figures. I ask Almighty God, the Glorious and Exalted, to elevate the rank of this great scholar and grant him the highest degrees of divine grace.
